newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down with softer weekend cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down with softer weekend cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Friday in a sluggish session, with reports of softer weekend physical prices pressuring the complex though values remained in recent technical ranges.
August slipped 2.9 cents to close at $2.146 per million British thermal units. September settled 2.2 cents lower at $2.096. Other deferreds ended down by 1.8 to 2.7 cents.

"Cash was a little weaker today but it came back. It still seems pretty well supported. Someone's got to blink next week," said one Midwest trader, referring to the seven cent cash premium to August with just two days left to expiry.
NYMEX August natgas futures expire Tuesday, July 29.

Chart traders agreed August remained stuck in a range, with support still seen at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance was now in the $2.20-21 area, with further selling likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.

Most traders noted there was little conviction about market direction. The bulls expect steady injection demand and favorable summer-to-winter spreads to support or firm prices, while the bears point to comfortable inventories and the lack of any extreme heat heading into August.
Temperatures in the Midwest and Northeast are forecast to briefly warm this weekend, then slip back to below-normal levels for most of next week.
Based on recent AGA storage data, weekly injections need to average 67 bcf to get stocks back to 2.8 tcf by end-October ahead of the peak demand winter season.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices slipped a couple of cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down a penny or two to the low-to-mid teens. New York city gate gas was also slightly lower at about $2.40.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 2.4 cents to $2.194.
On the KCBT, August finished up 3.5 cents at $2.10, while deferreds ended one to three cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
